Before attempting to solve this task, please follow these steps:

1. **Analyze the task requirements** and identify what domain knowledge, APIs, or techniques are needed.

2. **Write 1-5 modular skill documents** that would help solve this task. Each skill should:

4. **Then solve the task** using the skills you created as reference.

This approach tests your ability to identify and document relevant knowledge before applying it.

<project xmlns="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0" xmlns:xsi="http://www.w3.org/2001/XMLSchema-instance"
  xsi:schemaLocation="http://maven.apache.org/POM/4.0.0 http://maven.apache.org/maven-v4_0_0.xsd">
  <modelVersion>4.0.0</modelVersion>

  <parent>
    <groupId>org.sonatype.oss</groupId>
    <artifactId>oss-parent</artifactId>
    <version>7</version>
  </parent>

  <groupId>com.google.auto</groupId>
  <artifactId>auto-parent</artifactId>
  <packaging>pom</packaging>
  <version>3</version>
  <name>Auto (Parent)</name>
  <description>A collection of code generators for Java.</description>
  <url>https://github.com/google/auto</url>

  <properties>
    <project.build.sourceEncoding>UTF-8</project.build.sourceEncoding>
    <java.version>1.6</java.version>
  </properties>

  <scm>
    <url>http://github.com/google/auto</url>
    <connection>scm:git:git://github.com/google/auto.git</connection>
    <developerConnection>scm:git:ssh://git@github.com/google/auto.git</developerConnection>
    <tag>HEAD</tag>
  </scm>

  <issueManagement>
    <system>GitHub Issues</system>
    <url>http://github.com/google/auto/issues</url>
  </issueManagement>

  <licenses>
    <license>
      <name>Apache 2.0</name>
      <url>http://www.apache.org/licenses/LICENSE-2.0.txt</url>
    </license>
  </licenses>

  <organization>
    <name>Google, Inc.</name>
    <url>http://www.google.com</url>
  </organization>

  <build>
    <plugins>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
        <artifactId>maven-compiler-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>3.1</version>

          <source>${java.version}</source>
          <target>${java.version}</target>
          <compilerArgument>-Xlint:all</compilerArgument>
          <showWarnings>true</showWarnings>
          <showDeprecation>true</showDeprecation>
        </configuration>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
        <artifactId>maven-checkstyle-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>2.11</version>
        <configuration>
          <consoleOutput>true</consoleOutput>
          <configLocation>checkstyle.xml</configLocation>
          <failOnViolation>false</failOnViolation>

      <plugins>
        <plugin>
          <artifactId>maven-invoker-plugin</artifactId>
          <version>1.8</version>
        </plugin>
      </plugins>
    </pluginManagement>

        <toolsjar>${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar</toolsjar>

    <profile>

        <file>
          <exists>${java.home}/../Classes/classes.jar</exists>
        </file>
      </activation>
      <properties>
        <toolsjar>${java.home}/../Classes/classes.jar</toolsjar>
      </properties>
    </profile>
  </profiles>
</project>

    <tag>compile-testing-0.7</tag>
  </scm>
  <dependencies>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>junit</groupId>
      <artifactId>junit</artifactId>

      <activation>

      </activation>

            <version>1.4</version>

              </execution>
            </executions>
          </plugin>
          <plugin>
            <artifactId>maven-javadoc-plugin</artifactId>
            <version>2.8</version>
            <executions>
              <execution>
                <id>attach-docs</id>
                <goals><goal>jar</goal></goals>
              </execution>
            </executions>
          </plugin>
        </plugins>
      </build>
    </profile>
  </profiles>
</project>

content.text: Now I have a clear picture. The `compile-testing:0.7` dependency declares a system-scoped dependency on `com.sun:tools` using `${toolsjar}` which points to `tools.jar`. In Java 11, `tools.jar` doesn't exist (it was removed in Java 9). Let me now check all modules for similar issues and also look for any Java source code compilation errors.

# Maven tools.jar Compatibility for Java 9+

## Problem
In Java 8 and earlier, `tools.jar` (located at `$JAVA_HOME/lib/tools.jar`) contained the Java compiler API and annotation processing tools. Many Maven projects declared a system-scoped dependency on it:

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
  <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
  <version>${java.version}</version>
  <scope>system</scope>
  <systemPath>${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar</systemPath>
</dependency>
```

Starting with Java 9, `tools.jar` was removed. The classes were folded into the JDK modules (primarily `jdk.compiler` and `java.compiler`). This causes `DependencyResolutionException` errors when building old projects on Java 9+.

## Error Message
```
Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.x at specified path .../lib/tools.jar
```

## Solutions

### Solution 1: Add a Java 9+ Profile to Exclude tools.jar
Add a Maven profile activated on Java 9+ that provides the tools dependency as an empty/no-op:

```xml
<profiles>
  <!-- Java 8 and earlier: tools.jar exists -->
  <profile>
    <id>default-tools</id>
    <activation>
      <file>
        <exists>${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar</exists>
      </file>
    </activation>
    <dependencies>
      <dependency>
        <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
        <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
        <version>${java.version}</version>
        <scope>system</scope>
        <systemPath>${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar</systemPath>
      </dependency>
    </dependencies>
  </profile>
</profiles>
```

### Solution 2: Exclude com.sun:tools from Transitive Dependencies
When a dependency (like `compile-testing`) transitively pulls in `com.sun:tools`, exclude it:

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.google.testing.compile</groupId>
  <artifactId>compile-testing</artifactId>
  <version>0.7</version>
  <scope>test</scope>
  <exclusions>
    <exclusion>
      <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
      <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
    </exclusion>
  </exclusions>
</dependency>
```

### Solution 3: Set JAVA_HOME to a Java 8 JDK
If a JDK 8 is available, set the environment:
```bash
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-8-oracle
export PATH=$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH
```

### Solution 4: Upgrade Dependencies

```diff
--- a/path/to/file.txt
+++ b/path/to/file.txt
@@ -start,count +start,count @@
 context line
-removed line
+added line
 context line
```

## Format Elements

### File Headers
```diff
--- a/original/file.xml    (original file)
+++ b/modified/file.xml    (modified file)
```

### Hunk Headers
```diff
@@ -10,7 +10,15 @@
```

- `+10,15`: Starting at line 10 in modified, showing 15 lines

### Line Prefixes
- ` ` (space): Context line (unchanged)
- `-`: Removed line
- `+`: Added line

```bash

# Create diff for a git repository

diff -u -U3 original.xml modified.xml > patch.diff
```

```bash

# Apply with git

# Dry run (test without applying)

# Apply with fuzz factor (for slight mismatches)
patch -p1 -F3 < patch.diff

# Reverse a patch
patch -p1 -R < patch.diff
```

## Strip Level (-p flag)

- `-p1`: Strip first component (`src/main/File.java`) - most common with git diffs
- `-p2`: Strip two components (`main/File.java`)

```diff
+++ b/file1.xml
@@ -1,3 +1,4 @@
 line1
+new line
 line2
 line3

+++ b/file2.xml
@@ -5,3 +5,3 @@
 line5

+new line
 line7
```

```xml

  <exclusions>
```

# Maven tools.jar Compatibility for Java 9+

## Problem
In Java 8 and earlier, `tools.jar` (located at `$JAVA_HOME/lib/tools.jar`) contained the Java compiler API and annotation processing tools. Many Maven projects declared a system-scoped dependency on it:

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
  <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
  <version>${java.version}</version>
  <scope>system</scope>
  <systemPath>${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar</systemPath>
</dependency>
```

Starting with Java 9, `tools.jar` was removed. The classes were folded into the JDK modules (primarily `jdk.compiler` and `java.compiler`). This causes `DependencyResolutionException` errors when building old projects on Java 9+.

## Error Message
```
Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.x at specified path .../lib/tools.jar
```

## Solutions

### Solution 1: Add a Java 9+ Profile to Exclude tools.jar
Add a Maven profile activated on Java 9+ that provides the tools dependency as an empty/no-op:

```xml
<profiles>
  <!-- Java 8 and earlier: tools.jar exists -->
  <profile>
    <id>default-tools</id>
    <activation>
      <file>
        <exists>${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar</exists>
      </file>
    </activation>
    <dependencies>
      <dependency>
        <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
        <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
        <version>${java.version}</version>
        <scope>system</scope>
        <systemPath>${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar</systemPath>
      </dependency>
    </dependencies>
  </profile>
</profiles>
```

### Solution 2: Exclude com.sun:tools from Transitive Dependencies
When a dependency (like `compile-testing`) transitively pulls in `com.sun:tools`, exclude it:

```xml
<dependency>
  <groupId>com.google.testing.compile</groupId>
  <artifactId>compile-testing</artifactId>
  <version>0.7</version>
  <scope>test</scope>
  <exclusions>
    <exclusion>
      <groupId>com.sun</groupId>
      <artifactId>tools</artifactId>
    </exclusion>
  </exclusions>
</dependency>
```

### Solution 3: Set JAVA_HOME to a Java 8 JDK
If a JDK 8 is available, set the environment:
```bash
export JAVA_HOME=/usr/lib/jvm/java-8-oracle
export PATH=$JAVA_HOME/bin:$PATH
```

### Solution 4: Upgrade Dependencies
Newer versions of libraries like `compile-testing` (0.9+) removed the `tools.jar` dependency and use the module system instead.

## Key Points
- `tools.jar` was removed in Java 9 as part of the module system (Project Jigsaw)
- The classes from `tools.jar` are in `java.compiler` and `jdk.compiler` modules in Java 9+
- System-scoped dependencies with `<systemPath>` pointing to `tools.jar` will fail on Java 9+
- Profile-based activation using `<file><exists>` is the standard pattern for conditional inclusion

The integration test references `MoreObjects` from Guava, but the functional test POM doesn't have a direct Guava dependency (only `guava-testlib` as test scope). The `auto-value` jar uses the maven-shade-plugin to shade Guava, so `MoreObjects` wouldn't be available as `com.google.common.base.MoreObjects` - it would be under the shaded package.

The test needs a Guava dependency. Let me check what version of Guava provides `MoreObjects`:

The test imports `com.google.common.base.MoreObjects`, `ComparisonChain`, `ImmutableList`, `ImmutableMap`, `ImmutableSet`, `ImmutableTable` from Guava. These are all Guava core classes. The `guava-testlib` dependency provides test utilities, but the test also needs the core `guava` dependency. The functional POM is missing a `guava` dependency.

`MoreObjects` was added in Guava 18.0 (it was previously `Objects` in older versions). The test POM has `guava-testlib:18.0` which transitively pulls in `guava:18.0`, but let me check if it actually does:

BUILD FAILURE ANALYSIS
=====================

Repository: google/auto
Build command: mvn -B -U -f build-pom.xml verify

Two distinct errors cause the build to fail:

ERROR 1: com.sun:tools:jar dependency resolution failure
---------------------------------------------------------
Module: auto-common (and transitively all downstream modules)
Error message:
  "Could not find artifact com.sun:tools:jar:11.0.27 at specified path
   /usr/lib/jvm/java-11-openjdk-amd64/../lib/tools.jar"

Root cause:
  The compile-testing library (versions 0.6, 0.7, 0.8) used as a test
  dependency in auto-common, auto-service, auto-factory, and auto-value
  declares a system-scoped dependency on com.sun:tools with a systemPath
  pointing to ${java.home}/../lib/tools.jar.

  This tools.jar file existed in Java 8 and earlier but was removed in
  Java 9 as part of Project Jigsaw (the module system). The classes from
  tools.jar were incorporated into the java.compiler and jdk.compiler modules.

  The build environment runs Maven with Java 11 JRE (openjdk 11.0.27),
  which does not have tools.jar. Additionally, this is only a JRE (not JDK),
  so javac is not available either.

  However, Java 7 and Java 8 JDKs are installed on the system:
  - /usr/lib/jvm/java-7-openjdk-amd64 (JDK with tools.jar)
  - /usr/lib/jvm/java-8-oracle (JDK with tools.jar)

  The parent POM (pom.xml) has profiles for detecting tools.jar but they
  cannot resolve the issue because the file simply doesn't exist for Java 11.

Fix:
  Set JAVA_HOME to /usr/lib/jvm/java-8-oracle to use a JDK that has both
  javac and tools.jar. The project targets Java 1.6 source level, so Java 8
  is fully compatible.

  Additionally, as a defensive measure, exclude the com.sun:tools transitive
  dependency from compile-testing in module POMs and add a Java 9+ profile
  to the parent POM.


ERROR 2: MoreObjects class not found in integration test
---------------------------------------------------------
Module: auto-value (integration test: value/src/it/functional)
Error message:
  "cannot find symbol: class MoreObjects
   location: package com.google.common.base"
File: value/src/it/functional/src/test/java/com/google/auto/value/AutoValueTest.java:20

Root cause:
  The functional integration test imports com.google.common.base.MoreObjects
  (Guava class introduced in version 18.0). The test POM has guava-testlib:18.0
  (test scope) which transitively depends on guava:18.0. However, truth:0.25
  also depends on guava:17.0.

  Maven's dependency mediation uses "nearest wins" strategy. Since truth:0.25
  is declared before guava-testlib:18.0 in the POM, and truth's transitive
  guava:17.0 is at the same depth or nearer, Maven resolves guava to version
  17.0 instead of 18.0.

  MoreObjects does NOT exist in Guava 17.0 - it was introduced in 18.0.

Fix:
  Add a direct guava:18.0 dependency (test scope) to the functional integration
  test POM (value/src/it/functional/pom.xml). A direct dependency always wins
  over transitive dependencies in Maven's mediation.


FILES TO MODIFY:
  1. pom.xml - Add Java 9+ profile for tools.jar compatibility
  2. common/pom.xml - Exclude com.sun:tools from compile-testing
  3. service/pom.xml - Exclude com.sun:tools from compile-testing
  4. factory/pom.xml - Exclude com.sun:tools from compile-testing
  5. value/pom.xml - Exclude com.sun:tools from compile-testing

  </description>

  <properties>
    <guava.version>18.0</guava.version>
  </properties>
  <scm>
    <url>http://github.com/google/auto</url>

    <developerConnection>scm:git:ssh://git@github.com/google/auto.git</developerConnection>

  <dependencies>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.auto</groupId>
      <artifactId>auto-common</artifactId>

    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.auto.service</groupId>
      <artifactId>auto-service</artifactId>
      <version>1.0-rc2</version>
    </dependency>

      <groupId>com.google.guava</groupId>
      <artifactId>guava</artifactId>
      <version>${guava.version}</version>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.ow2.asm</groupId>
      <artifactId>asm</artifactId>
      <version>4.1</version>
    </dependency>
    <!-- test dependencies -->
    <dependency>
      <groupId>org.apache.velocity</groupId>
      <artifactId>velocity</artifactId>
      <version>1.7</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.guava</groupId>
      <artifactId>guava-testlib</artifactId>
      <version>${guava.version}</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.testing.compile</groupId>
      <artifactId>compile-testing</artifactId>
      <version>0.6</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>junit</groupId>
      <artifactId>junit</artifactId>
      <version>4.11</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
    <dependency>
      <groupId>com.google.truth</groupId>
      <artifactId>truth</artifactId>
      <version>0.25</version>
      <scope>test</scope>
    </dependency>
  </dependencies>

  <build>
    <resources>
      <resource>
        <directory>src/main/java</directory>
      </resource>
    </resources>
    <plugins>
      <plugin>
        <artifactId>maven-jar-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>2.5</version>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.apache.maven.plugins</groupId>
        <artifactId>maven-invoker-plugin</artifactId>
        <configuration>
          <addTestClassPath>true</addTestClassPath>
          <cloneProjectsTo>${project.build.directory}/it</cloneProjectsTo>
          <filterProperties>
            <auto.version>${project.version}</auto.version>
          </filterProperties>
          <pomIncludes>
            <pomInclude>*/pom.xml</pomInclude>
          </pomIncludes>
          <streamLogs>true</streamLogs>
        </configuration>
        <executions>
          <execution>
            <id>integration-test</id>
            <goals>
              <goal>install</goal>
              <goal>run</goal>
            </goals>
          </execution>
        </executions>
      </plugin>
      <plugin>
        <groupId>org.immutables.tools</groupId>
        <artifactId>maven-shade-plugin</artifactId>
        <version>3</version>
        <executions>
          <execution>
            <phase>package</phase>
            <goals>
              <goal>shade</goal>
            </goals>
            <configuration>
              <minimizeJar>true</minimizeJar>
              <relocations>
                <relocation>
                  <pattern>org.objectweb</pattern>
                  <shadedPattern>autovalue.shaded.org.objectweb$</shadedPattern>
                </relocation>
                <relocation>
                  <pattern>com.google</pattern>
                  <shadedPattern>autovalue.shaded.com.google$</shadedPattern>
                  <excludes>
                    <exclude>com.google.auto.value.**</exclude>
                  </excludes>
                </relocation>
              </relocations>
            </configuration>
          </execution>
        </executions>
      </plugin>
    </plugins>
  </build>
</project>

content.text:
Now there's a new issue in the `auto-factory` module - the tests are failing because `com/sun/tools/javac/api/JavacTool` cannot be found. This is because we excluded `com.sun:tools` from `compile-testing` in the factory module, but the factory tests actually need it at runtime for annotation processing tests.

The fix for factory is to NOT exclude `com.sun:tools` since Java 8's `tools.jar` is available, OR we need to add a profile-based dependency. Actually, the issue is that `compile-testing:0.8` needs `tools.jar` at runtime for its `JavacTool`. With Java 8 and the exclusion, the tool classes aren't on the classpath.

Let me reconsider the approach. Since we're using Java 8 which has `tools.jar`, we should NOT exclude `com.sun:tools` from `compile-testing` when running with Java 8. The exclusion is only needed for Java 9+. But the parent POM already has profiles that set `${toolsjar}` based on whether `tools.jar` exists.

The problem is: with Java 8 and the exclusion, the system-scoped `com.sun:tools` that `compile-testing` normally provides is gone. The `JavacTool` class lives in `tools.jar`.

Let me revert the exclusion for factory and instead just let it use the tools.jar naturally:

content.text:
Good, all the exclusions are reverted. Now the approach is:

1. The `com.sun:tools` issue is fixed by using Java 8 (JAVA_HOME)
2. The Guava `MoreObjects` issue is fixed by the direct dependency addition in the functional POM

But we still need to fix the parent POM so the build doesn't fail with Java 11. The `compile-testing` library's system-scoped dependency on `tools.jar` is the issue. Since we can't exclude it (tests need it), the fix is to provide `tools.jar` as a dependency in each module POM through a profile, or better yet, just fix the parent POM's profile to provide the `tools.jar` dependency.

Actually, looking more carefully at the build error: the `compile-testing` POM uses `${toolsjar}` which is set by profiles that check for file existence. On Java 11, neither `tools.jar` nor `classes.jar` exist, so no profile is activated, and `${toolsjar}` is empty. Maven then tries to resolve a system dependency with an invalid path.

The real fix needs to be: add `tools.jar` as a system dependency in the parent POM's profile (the one that activates when `tools.jar` exists). But the system dep in `compile-testing` is the problem - it's in a published artifact's POM that we can't change.
